supportingArgument.rationale: The reviewed manuscript separates AI-assisted research that may improve future model generations from fixed-model agent loops that iteratively improve ordinary software without changing the underlying model.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The OpenAI developer-issued High classification, Vals task-specific benchmark, Ondrej creator promotion and GhostMesh analysis have distinct roles and limitations; neither one certifies fully autonomous research.

counterargument.rationale: Research assistants and persistent coding agents may produce useful gains, and independent model review can catch errors, but these improvements do not imply autonomous release authority or universal safety.

tradeoffs.rationale: Higher iteration throughput is weighed against erroneous feedback, correlated reviewer blind spots, unverified changes, operator cost, approval boundaries and rollback responsibility.

falsifiability.rationale: The article proposes bounded research and coding replications using independent grading, controlled baselines, intervention logs and accepted production outcomes without claiming these tests were performed.

originalSynthesis.rationale: Four source-bounded figures depict two feedback loops, Astra versus Sol threshold interpretation, correlated model-review failures and a five-stage authority staircase without inventing measurements.

performance.rationale: The reviewer cross-checked OpenAI system-card OECI 170.1 versus 168.4 and the nuance of High classification; Vals task rankings differ and do not establish an autonomous research-production system.

economics.rationale: Cloudroom productivity and commercial revenue or valuation assertions are treated as unverified creator or vendor claims; no independently measured software throughput or return on investment is inferred.

threatGovernance.rationale: The argument separates agent patch proposals from release permission, unit tests from behavioral acceptance, model agreement from independent assurance, and controlled escalation from unrestricted autonomy.
